info.bio:
Marilyn Manson es un grupo de metal industrial de Estados Unidos surgido en 1989 en Fort Lauderdale, Florida. En un principio, Manson escribía poesías, pero al ver que sus poemas no caían bien, y siguiendo el consejo de la gente que escuchaba sus poemas, decidió ponerles música y transformarlas en canciones.

El líder y fundador del grupo es Marilyn Manson, cuyo nombre real es Brian Warner. La elección de este nombre, corresponde a la fusión entre la actriz Marilyn Monroe y el asesino Charles Manson

scenes.name: La bestia ha vuelto: OzzFest y las reuniones
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: A finales de siglo el metal vuelve a la corriente principal. Con el alternativo moribundo y la electrónica sin despegar, el público fiel sigue ahí: tres mil personas esperan cinco horas en un centro comercial de Chicago en 1998 a que Black Sabbath les firme discos. El detonante es el OzzFest de 1997, organizado por la mánager de Ozzy, que vende más que Lollapalooza con Pantera, Machine Head, Fear Factory, Type O Negative, Neurosis, tres cuartas partes de Black Sabbath y Marilyn Manson, cuyas provocaciones atraen protestas cristianas y titulares. Metallica vuelve a tocar su thrash en directo y en Garage Inc.; Judas Priest ficha a Tim «Ripper» Owens, cantante de una banda tributo llamada British Steel; Mötley Crüe recupera a Vince Neil, Kiss se reúne en 1998, Dickinson regresa a Iron Maiden y Black Sabbath hace en 1999 una gira de reunión con disco de oro. Weinstein ve en ese regreso el gusto «prole» de la cultura de fin de siglo, un contrapeso a la feminización del pop y la ansiedad milenarista: la bestia se niega a morir.

scenes.name: Metal de los noventa: progresivo, death y black metal
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Si los ochenta fueron la edad de oro del heavy metal, los noventa lo fragmentan en estilos que amplían ideas anteriores. El pop-metal (Warrant, Extreme, Live) es lo menos significativo; Marilyn Manson casa el scum-rock de Alice Cooper con el industrial de Nine Inch Nails. El metal progresivo (Warrior Soul, Dream Theater, Royal Hunt, Opeth, los suizos Alboth!). El death metal muta en algo más terrible y más musical gracias a Brutal Truth, Cannibal Corpse y, sobre todo, la tríada de Type O Negative (Slow Deep And Hard, misas negras wagnerianas), Today Is The Day y Fear Factory; Biohazard, Coalesce, Dillinger Escape Plan. El nuevo black metal escandinavo: Entombed, Darkthrone, Immortal, Mayhem, Enslaved, Emperor, Satyricon, Cradle Of Filth.

podcast.title: Blizzard Stranded with Sesame Street Cast – Allentown, Pennsylvania, January 6, 1996
podcast.body: After a Marilyn Manson show at Stars in Allentown, Pennsylvania, on January 6, 1996, a severe blizzard dumped three feet of snow on the area, stranding everyone in their hotel. Also stranded in the same hotel were Shaquille O'Neal and members of the Orlando Magic basketball team, and the entire cast of *Sesame Street Live*, including performers playing Bert, Ernie, Oscar the Grouch, the Cookie Monster, and Big Bird. With nowhere else to go, the band, the basketball team, and the Sesame Street characters gathered in the hotel bar, drank heavily, and sang songs together until three in the morning. "With nowhere else to go, the band, the team, the cast of Sesame Street... they all gathered in the bar, drank very heavily and sang songs together until three in the morning."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sheraton Hotel Destruction (1998)
podcast.body: In 1998, Marilyn Manson and his crew extensively damaged four rooms and set some fires at the Sheraton hotel in Poughkeepsie, New York. The total damage from their actions amounted to $25,000. "In 1998, Marilyn Manson and his crew went to town at the Sheraton in Poukeepsie, New York."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Columbine School Shooting Misinformation (1999)
podcast.body: Following the Columbine school shootings, false reports spread that the shooters wore Marilyn Manson makeup and t-shirts and were big fans of his music, despite these stories being completely misinformed. This misinformation caused a massive blowback, leading to death threats and cancelled shows, and nearly ruined him professionally and personally. "Things peaked after the Columbine school shootings when it was reported that the shooters were wearing Maryland Manson makeup and t-shirts and were big fans of Manson's music. Now, that was not true. It did not happen that way."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: The Matrix Soundtrack Contribution (1999)
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson was featured on the first *Matrix* soundtrack, released in 1999. The album was characterized by "really cool heavy stuff," including contributions from other heavy acts like Ministry, The Prodigy, Rammstein, and Rage Against the Machine. "It was some really cool heavy stuff, Marilyn Manson, Ministry of the Prodigy, Ramstein, Rage Against the Machine."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Abundant Tattoos
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson is noted for having "a ton" of tattoos, suggesting extensive body art. "And Marilyn Manson has a ton."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Accusations of Promoting Violence and Columbine Behavior
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson was accused by critics of promoting hate, violence, suicide, death, drug use, and behavior akin to the Columbine massacre, with opponents vowing to fight against his presence. "Si Maril y Manson puede venir a nuestra ciudad y promover el odio, la violencia, el suicidio, la muerte, el consumo de drogas y un comportamiento como el de Columbine, yo puedo decir, no lo conseguirás sin antes pelear."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Cómo Marilyn Manson revolucionó el mundo con Antichrist Superstar

podcast.title: Alleged Drug Use with Human Remains
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson has been associated with numerous strange and controversial acts, including the allegation that he smoked drugs which had been reportedly cut with human remains. "Marilyn Manson, who's been known for many weird things, including allegedly smoking drugs that had been cut with human remains."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Anti-Christian Antics
podcast.body: Manson has been outspoken against Christianity, sometimes tearing pages out of a Bible during concerts to shock audiences. "And Manson hasn't exactly been kind when it came to Christianity. In concert, he'd sometimes tear pages out of a Bible. So again, shocking."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Artistic Sensibility
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson is mentioned among a group of bands that possess an inherent artistic sensibility without being "over the top," often attributed to members having attended art school, studied art, or collected art. "You too, the cure, Marilyn Manson, Roxy Music, the Sex Pistols, Blur, they all get it without going over the top, mainly because each one of them either A went to art school, or B studied art, or C collect art."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Franz Ferdinand: In Their Own Words

podcast.title: Association with Trent Reznor
podcast.body: Trent Reznor's association with Marilyn Manson during his period of deep depression and addiction "certainly didn't help" his struggles. "hanging out with his new buddy Marilyn Manson, certainly didn't help."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Association with Violence
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson's music has been controversially mentioned as a favorite of shooters in school incidents, notably the Columbine High School shooting, which significantly vilified Goth culture. "Why is it that whenever there's a school shooting, Marilyn Manson's music is mentioned as a favorite of the shooter or the shooters?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Autobiographical Trilogy in Reverse
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson created a conceptual trilogy across three records (*Antichrist Superstar*, *Mechanical Animals*, *Holy Wood*) that collectively form his autobiography, but uniquely told in reverse order of his life's progression. Each album also has its own individual conceptual plot points. "Three of his records form a conceptual trilogy. Although it's not necessarily obvious."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Backmasking in Digital Era
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson is cited for employing backward messages in recordings, a technique that saw a resurgence from the late 1990s and early 2000s with digital sound editing. "Back, cake, cold play, M&M, Fransford Nand, Lincoln Park, Marilyn Manson, Moby Soundgarden Tool, 21 Pilots, and a ton more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Birth of the "Grotesque Spectacle"
podcast.body: While Marilyn Manson always had a grotesque aspect to his shows, the "Antichrist Superstar" era is identified as the moment the "grotesque spectacle" truly emerged in capital letters for the band. "es aquí cuando nace el espectáculo grotesco en mayúsculas por parte de Mel y Manzo."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Cómo Marilyn Manson revolucionó el mundo con Antichrist Superstar

podcast.title: Blame for Columbine Killings
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson received significant blame in the aftermath of the Columbine killings in Colorado on April 20, 1999, because the two perpetrators were reportedly fans of his music. This association led to him being "unwelcome in Colorado for years after that." "Marilyn Manson took a lot of blame in that case because apparently the two killers were fans of his. He was unwelcome in Colorado for years after that."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Body Modification Myths
podcast.body: Several myths circulate about Marilyn Manson's body, including claims that he tattooed his private parts black, had breast implants, pulled audience members on stage for sex, or distributed puppies to the audience to be torn apart on cue. All of these claims are false. "Manson also did not tattoo his private bits black. He did not have breast implants, pull someone from the audience to have sex with on stage, or distribute puppies to the audience to be torn apart on cue."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Breaking Barriers, Influenced by Ozzy Osbourne
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson broke many barriers during this period, in a way not seen since Ozzy Osbourne, being heavily inspired by Osbourne's absolute and sometimes gratuitous provocation. "rompe muchísimas barreras que yo creo que nadie sabía trevida sobre pasar desde Osi Osborn."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Cómo Marilyn Manson revolucionó el mundo con Antichrist Superstar

podcast.title: Christian Protests and Political Opposition
podcast.body: The release of "Antichrist Superstar" led to magnified controversy, including Christian demonstrations outside Marilyn Manson's concerts and issues with members of the U.S. Senate. "empezaron todas esas manifestaciones cristianas a la puerta de los conciertos de Mey Manson e incluso llóganse a tener problemas con algunos miembros del Senado de los Estados Unidos."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Cómo Marilyn Manson revolucionó el mundo con Antichrist Superstar

podcast.title: Columbine Massacre Association
podcast.body: For years, Marilyn Manson was the target of severe criticism and attacks from American society, with conservative movements attempting to link him to the Columbine massacre, especially through claims that the perpetrators listened to his music. "hubo movimientos conservadores que intentaron ligar a Meli Manzon con la macabra matanza de Columbine, porque los chavales que habían hecho la matanza de Columbine en el documental bowling en el recorrer de Meli Manzon."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Cómo Marilyn Manson revolucionó el mundo con Antichrist Superstar

podcast.title: Complex Persona
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson's image is extreme, but the individual (Brian Warner) is described as "very well read, very well spoken," creating a powerful attraction for diverse fans. "Marilyn Manson's music image is pretty extreme. At the same time, Manson himself is very well read, very well spoken."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Concert Cancellations Following Tragedy
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson cancelled the last five concerts of his national tour out of respect for the victims of the Littleton tragedy (implied Columbine), demonstrating a sensitivity amid controversy. "Han cancelado los últimos cinco conciertos de su gira nacional por respeto a los caídos en Lita el Ton."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Cómo Marilyn Manson revolucionó el mundo con Antichrist Superstar

podcast.title: Contemporary Glam Trappings
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson is listed as an act exhibiting "Glam trappings" in their music and visual style, demonstrating glam's ongoing influence in later decades. "Look at acts like Marilyn Manson."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Glam Rock

podcast.title: Critique of Broader Societal Moral Structures
podcast.body: Beyond the direct critique of religion, Marilyn Manson also uses *Antichrist Superstar* to challenge various societal structures that impose morality. This includes the law, police, state structures, and government, arguing against any system that dictates what is "correct" and "incorrect" rather than allowing individuals to forge their own moral understanding. "Mery Manson critica la ley, critica la policía, critica las estructuras del Estado, critica las estructuras de gobierno, critica todo lo que construye, lo que es la moralidad social o lo que nos genera esa idea de lo que es correcto y no es correcto, que no nacemos con ella sino que no es la inculcante de pequeños."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Antichrist Superstar: Marilyn Manson y la filosofía

podcast.title: Critique of Social Stereotypes, not Religion Itself
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson's critique was aimed at social stereotypes, including those associated with Christian and Catholic religions, rather than an obsession against religion in general. "Marilim Manzon no tenía una obsesión en contra de la redición cristiana, nicatólica, ni la redición general, sino en contra de muchos esterotipos sociales entre ellos esa."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Cómo Marilyn Manson revolucionó el mundo con Antichrist Superstar

podcast.title: Current Artistic Pursuits
podcast.body: Today, Marilyn Manson continues his artistic endeavors, having branched out into painting and acting in both film and television. "Manson today continues to do his thing, although he's branched out into art, he paints, and acting in both film and television."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death Threats from Conservative and Radical Christian Groups
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson received death threats from conservative elements and especially from radical Christian movements during the controversial period of "Antichrist Superstar." "Mel y Manzo, un llegó a ser amenazado de muerte para algunos miembros, sus reconcervadores y sobre todo por movimientos cristianos radicales."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Cómo Marilyn Manson revolucionó el mundo con Antichrist Superstar

podcast.title: Denial of Blame for Violence
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson explicitly stated that artists like him should not be blamed for violent acts such as the Columbine massacre, refuting the accusations made against him. "el cantante afirma que no es artista como él, a quienes hay que culpar."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Cómo Marilyn Manson revolucionó el mundo con Antichrist Superstar

podcast.title: Donna's Domain Review
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson was "described as being lame" on Donna's Domain, a website that rates rock stars' penis size and sexual ability. This assessment suggests an unfavorable evaluation by the website's critics. "Marilyn Manson, however, is described as being lame."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Embalmed Makeup Look
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson is recognized for pioneering a distinctive "embalmed" makeup look, which became a signature part of his provocative and theatrical image. "to the embalmed look of Marilyn Manson."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: End of Close Relationship with Trent Reznor
podcast.body: The "Antichrist Superstar" era marked, in part, the end of the very close working relationship between Marilyn Manson and Trent Reznor, though their mutual influence continued. "fue el final de esa relación tan cerrada que había entre Meli Manzon y el Rennor."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Cómo Marilyn Manson revolucionó el mundo con Antichrist Superstar

podcast.title: Evil Appearance
podcast.body: He cultivated an evil image through corpse paint makeup and weird contact lenses, deliberately trying to look as malevolent as possible. "And the corpse paint makeup and the weird contact lenses didn't help. He deliberately tried to look as evil as possible."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Evolution of Grotesque Spectacle
podcast.body: The "Antichrist Superstar" tour marked a pivotal point where Marilyn Manson further developed and deepened his commitment to grotesque performance spectacle, building on previous inclinations. "adentro más por un lado a la polémica y por el otro lado a Mel y Manzo a profundizar más sobre el espectáculo grotesco."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Cómo Marilyn Manson revolucionó el mundo con Antichrist Superstar

podcast.title: Extreme Artistic Approach
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson pushed artistic boundaries to extreme limits, even compromising his own health, during the creation of "Antichrist Superstar." "lleva el trabajo artístico a unos límites que yo creo que casi no habíamos visto."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Cómo Marilyn Manson revolucionó el mundo con Antichrist Superstar

podcast.title: Extreme Image & Pseudonyms
podcast.body: The band cultivated a "spooky looking group" image, all dressed in black, with each member adopting a pseudonym that incorporated the name of a serial killer. "each adopting a pseudonym that included the name of a serial killer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Extreme Self-Harm and Drug Use
podcast.body: During the lyrical composition of "Antichrist Superstar," Marilyn Manson engaged in severe self-harm, including piercing himself with needles and hitting himself, all while in a mentally deteriorated state exacerbated by extensive drug use. "como hacerse daño con agujas, me refiero clavarse cosas, martiliarse, llegó a hacerse verdadero dolor físico en un estado mental verdaderamente deteriorado por el Fue Toda Norgia de Droga, tremenda."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Cómo Marilyn Manson revolucionó el mundo con Antichrist Superstar

podcast.title: Fans Sue Government Over Concert Bans
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson's fans took legal action, suing the government for prohibiting his concerts, a testament to their dedication and the legal battles surrounding the band. "fans de Mel y Manzo que llegaron a demás que llegaron a demandar al gobierno por haber prohibido el concierto de Mel y Manzo."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Cómo Marilyn Manson revolucionó el mundo con Antichrist Superstar

podcast.title: Featured on Big Shiny Toons 2
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson was one of the artists featured on Much Music's *Big Shiny Toons 2*, an alt-rock compilation released in 1997. The album's success, selling over 1.2 million units in Canada, demonstrated the broad appeal of artists within the alternative rock genre. "featuring the prodigy, blur, Marilyn Manson, Bush, Collective Soul, the Tea Party, Radiohead, Stone Temple Pilots, and more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Future of the Music Video - Part 2

podcast.title: Feud with Trent Reznor
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson and Trent Reznor, who were once good friends, became "mortal enemies" after Manson's behavior allegedly became "way too weird and sick" for Reznor. "Treg Resner versus Marilyn Manson. They used to be good buddies, but it appears that Manson got way too weird and sick for trans-liking."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Florida Goth Scene Product
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson later emerged from a serious goth scene that developed in Florida, indicating the regional diversification of the genre's influence. "A serious Goth scene developed in Florida, one that would later give us Marilyn Manson"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Genre Ambiguity
podcast.body: The band's genre classification as Goth or Industrial is ambiguous, often depending on which Goths are asked, reflecting a blend of both yet also being neither exclusively. "So as Manson, Goth or Industrial, a bit of both really and neither actually, and all depends on which Goths you ask."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Global Breakthrough with Antichrist Superstar
podcast.body: A significant portion of the world outside the United States discovered Marilyn Manson through "Antichrist Superstar," establishing him as an unstoppable phenomenon. "una parte muy importante del mundo fuera de Estados Unidos, conocí a Mel y Manzo en la parte de Anticristos Superestar y ya el fenomeno era imparable."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Cómo Marilyn Manson revolucionó el mundo con Antichrist Superstar

podcast.title: Goth/Industrial/Death Metal Mix
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson is presented as a contemporary example of Goth going industrial, influenced by Goth, industrial bands like Nine Inch Nails and Skinny Puppy, and intense Florida death metal. "Cross that with a love for industrial bands like nine-inch nails and skinny puppy and an admiration for intense Florida death metal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence of Jewish Band Members
podcast.body: The presence of references to Judaism and inspirations from the Jewish Kabbalah within *Antichrist Superstar*, particularly in the album's booklet, is attributed in part to the Jewish background of some members of Marilyn Manson's band. "Esto también se debe a que parte algunos de los miembros de la banda de Mery Manson era del edición judío."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Antichrist Superstar: Marilyn Manson y la filosofía

podcast.title: Influence of Kafka's *The Metamorphosis*
podcast.body: In addition to Nietzsche, Marilyn Manson incorporates significant influences from Franz Kafka's *The Metamorphosis* into *Antichrist Superstar*. This influence is particularly evident in the album's macabre and destructive vision of human transformation, where the individual becomes a monstrous entity, diverging from Nietzsche's concept of the valiant Superhombre. "En el caso de Emelie Manson trae influencias, no solo de Nietzsche, sino que ya trae muchas influencias sobre todo de la metamorfosis de Kafka."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Antichrist Superstar: Marilyn Manson y la filosofía

podcast.title: Influenced by Bauhaus
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson's sound and image were significantly shaped by the music and aesthetics of Bauhaus. "And if it weren't for them, there probably wouldn't be a... Maryland Manson."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus

podcast.title: Influenced by Bauhaus
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson would likely list Bauhaus as an influence, as the Goth pioneers' sound, look, and attitude spread globally, ultimately influencing bands like Marilyn Manson. "How would Marilyn Manson respond?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus?

podcast.title: Inspired by Skinny Puppy
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson is explicitly listed as an artist who was inspired and influenced by the Canadian industrial band Skinny Puppy. "Here's a short list of artists who say they were inspired and influenced by Skinny Puppy, Ministry, Nine-inch Nails, Maryland Manson, the Prodigy, Ramstein, Filter, Corn, Lincoln Park, Evan Essence."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Irony of Public Reaction to Thematic Shift
podcast.body: Ironically, despite the underlying message and critique remaining consistent, public concern about Marilyn Manson diminished significantly once he stopped explicitly naming religion in his criticisms. "como ya no ponía en nombre de religión ya nadie le importaba."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Cómo Marilyn Manson revolucionó el mundo con Antichrist Superstar

podcast.title: Josh Saviano Myth
podcast.body: A common myth claims that Marilyn Manson is actually a grown-up version of child actor Josh Saviano, who played Paul Fyfer on the TV show "The Wonder Years." This is factually incorrect; Saviano is now a lawyer. "The most common Manson myth that he's actually a grown-up version of child actor Josh Saviano, who played Paul Fyfer on the Wonder Years. That is totally incorrect, not true."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Louisiana Proposed Law – Fines Up to $2,000 for Selling a Marilyn Manson CD to a Minor
podcast.body: A proposed Louisiana law sought to prohibit the sale of "lyrics harmful to minors," defining "harmful" broadly to include topics such as rape, incest, and suicide. It would have imposed fines of up to $2,000 for selling a Marilyn Manson CD to a person under 17 who was unmarried. "Would have imposed fines of up to $2,000 for selling a Marilyn Manson CD to a minor under 17 who was not married."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mac Cosmetics Endorser
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson uses Mac Cosmetics, making the brand a preferred choice among musicians known for their theatrical makeup. This association further solidified Mac Cosmetics' reputation within the alternative music scene. "Marilyn Manson's brand and it's also the choice of the Cures Robert Smith makeup brand."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mainstream Backlash from Early Fans
podcast.body: "Antichrist Superstar" represented a significant shift for the band into the mainstream, leading some classic, closed-minded metal fans to hate Marilyn Manson simply for gaining wider visibility, despite the continued quality of the music. "hubo como una parte de esos fanáticos clásicos del metal cerrado, que no les gusta que parte de su música salta al mainstream, con lo cual pasearon a odiarlo solo porque salía el antivillo, creo, porque Meli Manzon siguió manteniendo nivel de calidad muy bueno."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Cómo Marilyn Manson revolucionó el mundo con Antichrist Superstar

podcast.title: Major Label Artist via Vanity Imprint
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson is cited as a major label artist who recorded through Nothing Records, which was a vanity boutique label subsidiary of Interscope Records, itself a part of the major label stable of Universal Records. This complex structure illustrates how major labels can integrate artists under seemingly independent imprints. "Marilyn Manson, a major label artist who recorded through nothing records, a vanity boutique label subsidiary of Interscope Records, which in turn is part of the major label stable that is Universal Records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mansinth – Marilyn Manson's Absinthe Brand
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson launched his own brand of absinthe called Mansinth, which is produced in Germany. Absinthe, historically known for its psychoactive reputation and associated with figures like Oscar Wilde and Vincent Van Gogh, experienced a revival in the 1990s. Mansinth garnered significant acclaim, winning a gold medal at the San Francisco World's Spirits Competition in March 2008. The product is described as expensive and was not available in Canada at the time of the discussion. "Mansinth is Marilyn Manson's brand, which is made in Germany and it is absolutely brilliant."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Philosophical Inspiration from Nietzsche
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson's creative process, particularly for *Antichrist Superstar*, is deeply rooted in philosophical concepts, with Friedrich Nietzsche being a paramount influence. Manson draws inspiration from Nietzsche's ideas on the Superhombre (Superman) and the overcoming of human limitations, as explored in works like *Thus Spoke Zarathustra*, *The Antichrist*, and *Ecce Homo*. "Mi inspiración siempre viene de algo como filosófico, como Nietzsche, como cartuní, como Willy Wonka."

podcast.title: Philosophical and Satanic Influences
podcast.body: Manson delved deeply into the philosophies of Satanist Aleister Crowley and the writings of Friedrich Nietzsche, and formed a friendship with Anton LaVey, the head of the Church of Satan, in which Manson is also a minister (though he doesn't take this seriously). "Manson himself got deep into the philosophies of Satanist, Alistair Crowley, and the writings of the uncompromising Frederick Nietzsche. He formed a friendship with Anton Leve, the head of the Church of Satan. Now, Manson is actually a minister in that church, but he doesn't take that seriously, just so you know."

podcast.title: Rationale for Religious Critiques
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson faced controversy for the direct attacks on Christianity in *Antichrist Superstar*, yet he also referenced other religions like Judaism. He explained that his focus on Christianity stemmed from his upbringing in a predominantly Christian environment, making it the system he felt he understood best to critique. He also noted that some band members were of Jewish background, informing the Jewish references. Manson chose not to attack Islam because he believed it was already sufficiently demonized by American and Western society and did not require further artistic demonization. "Mery Manson, además nos ha respondido sorprendentemente bien porque no decía que él había vivido un mentor reminente cristiano, él tenía a otros miembros que habían venido de religiones judaicas con lo cual se sentía que es lo que dominaba y lo que podía atacar. Y también consideraba que las religiones ya del ejemo en Solman, las religiones en Solman, ya estaban suficientemente demonizadas por la sociedad americana, la sociedad occidental en general que ya no necesitaba el indagar más en lo que era la demonización de las religiones en Solman."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Reinterpretation of Nietzsche's Path to Liberation
podcast.body: Marilyn Manson interprets Nietzsche's journey of human liberation in his own distinct way, creating a vision that is almost as compelling as Nietzsche's original, despite being nearly a century apart. Manson's version of this path is characterized by a darker and more macabre perspective. "Emelie Manson coge toda la idea de Nietzsche y hace su propia interpretación de ese camino de la liberación del hombre. Y la visión que hace Emelie Manson es casi tan apasionante como la que haría el propio Nietzsche hacía casi 100 años atrás."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Rib Removal Rumor – Denied; Floating Ribs Can Be Surgically Removed but Manson Did Not Have It Done
podcast.body: One of the most enduring Marilyn Manson rumors is that he had his lowest ribs removed to facilitate auto-erotic self-gratification. Floating ribs (numbers 11 and 12) do not extend all the way around to the breastbone and can be surgically removed — a procedure sometimes done for women alongside tummy tucks to create an hourglass figure. The same rumor has been attributed to Cher, Pamela Anderson, Kate Moss, Janet Jackson, and Britney Spears. However, Manson categorically did not have this done. The rumor persists purely because he has never worked to dispel the myth, preferring to let the mystery stand. "Because Manson is so weird in the first place, it's understandable why people would believe this rumor."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Ribs Removal Myth

He describes his beliefs as a personal interpretation incorporating diverse influences. "I'm not and never have been a spokesperson for Satanism. It's simply part of what I believe in along with Dr. Seuss, Dr. Hook, Nietzsche, and the Bible. I just have my own interpretation."

podcast.body: A Texas organization called the Crime Prevention Resource Center classified fans of Marilyn Manson and goth-rock in the same category as gang members, accusing them of drug use, vandalism, and "ritual sacrifices." podcast.title: Trilogy Chronological Interpretation
podcast.body: Interpreting the trilogy backwards reveals Manson's autobiographical intent: starting as an untainted suburban individual (*Holy Wood*'s Adam Cadmon), then shaped by American culture (guns, God, government), rebelling by forming a band and engaging in depravity (*Mechanical Animals*' Omega), potentially with Trent Reznor as a mentor (Alpha), and finally emerging as a logical, unfeeling "survival of the fittest Superman" (*Antichrist Superstar*'s Antichrist Superstar). "All starts to make sense, don't I?"

xref.title: Godfathers of Goth - Enduring Influence
xref.body: Bauhaus is widely recognized as one of the founding groups and pioneers of the original British Goth movement. Their distinctive glamour, energy, art school sensibilities, and attitude of "doom and gloom" had a profound and infectious impact globally, influencing numerous dark bands, including Nine Inch Nails, Marilyn Manson, White Zombie, Courtney Love, and The Smashing Pumpkins. "The band often described as the Godfathers of Goth."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Influence on Marilyn Manson
xref.body: Similarities between David Bowie's Ziggy Stardust and his film *The Man Who Fell to Earth* and Marilyn Manson's album *Mechanical Animals* (specifically Manson's character Omega) are completely intentional. "Many similarity to David Bowie's Ziggie Stardust in his film The Man Who Filled Earth is completely intentional."

xref.title: Influence on Marilyn Manson
xref.body: Members of Nine Inch Nails, including Trent Reznor and Sean Beavan, were instrumental in producing Marilyn Manson's early work and "Antichrist Superstar," bringing their industrial rock sound and production expertise. "Toda la parte de la discora fía anterior de Mey Manson esos dos trabajos anteriores, tenía un apoyo muy importante por Nine in Shnails, por tren Retnor que es el que había producido los trabajos anteriores en Mey Manson."

xref.title: Influence on Marilyn Manson
xref.body: Marilyn Manson admired industrial bands like Skinny Puppy. "Cross that with a love for industrial bands like nine-inch nails and skinny puppy"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Personal Struggles and Grandmother's Death (Mid-Late 1990s)
xref.body: Trent Reznor suffered from depression and a social anxiety disorder. The death of his grandmother, who raised him, profoundly affected him, leading to heavy drinking, cocaine use, and ultimately heroin addiction by the late 1990s. His association with Marilyn Manson during this period was also noted as unhelpful. "The death of his grandmother, the woman who raised him really messed him up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Producers for Chris Cornell's Solo Album – Launchpad for Other Gigs
xref.body: The group Eleven, comprising Elaine Johannes and Natasha Schneider, played a crucial role in producing Chris Cornell's debut solo record, *Euphoria Morning*. Their work on this album garnered them further producing gigs for notable artists like No Doubt and Josh Homme's Desert Session projects, connecting them to members of A Perfect Circle, Nine Inch Nails, Danzig, Marilyn Manson's band, and PJ Harvey. "Chris reliant on both of them to help produce his debut solo record Euphoria Morning... who, based on this work, got producing gigs for no doubt in Josh Hommie in the early days of his desert session projects."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Robert Smith's Preference for MAC Cosmetics
xref.body: Robert Smith of The Cure is noted as a loyal customer of MAC Cosmetics, a brand favored by performers like Marilyn Manson. This preference is attributed to MAC products' ability to hold up well under the hot lights of a stage. "A lot of performers like Manson and Robert Smith are the cure for Mac because it holds up nicely under hot stage lights."
